items.title: Jio IPO, India's largest public issue, opens for subscription
items.author: Smriti Jain
items.text:
Jio Platforms IPO: India’s largest Initial Public Offering (IPO) till date opens for subscription on Wednesday. Jio Platforms plans to raise approximately Rs 30,213 crore through a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares. The public issue opens on October 21 and will remain available for subscription until October 23. This marks RIL Group's first IPO in nearly two decades. Reliance Industries Ltd, led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, will continue to hold a majority stake in Jio Platforms following its stock market listing. From Jio IPO price band, listing date to GMP, we take a look at 10 important facts about the Jio IPO and what brokerages are saying:

...

## Jio IPO price band

The company has fixed the price band at Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share. Based on the offer documents, the IPO values the company at around $108 billion. Investors will be able to apply for Jio Platforms shares in lots of 12, or in multiples of 12 shares. The company is also seeking to widen access to its IPO by setting aside portions of the issue for different investor groups. Eligible Reliance Industries shareholders have a reservation of up to Rs 2,500 crore, while eligible employees can apply under a reservation of up to Rs 500 crore. 

Retail individual investors will be eligible to subscribe to at least 35 per cent of the net offer.

## Jio IPO listing date

Jio Platforms will list on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) on October 28, 2026.

...

Jio Platforms has allotted shares worth Rs 8,109.85 crore to 212 anchor investors at Rs 1,119 apiece, which is the upper end of its IPO’s price band. Institutional bids for the offering crossed a whopping Rs 2.5 lakh crore, which is more than 30 times the value of shares on offer in the anchor book. The company has allocated 7.24 crore shares. The scale of demand points to strong institutional interest in what is expected to be India's largest IPO. Life Insurance Corporation of India was the biggest recipient in the anchor allotment, securing shares worth Rs 499.98 crore. New World Fund Inc received shares of Rs 486.27 crore, while the Government of Singapore was allotted Rs 340.93 crore. SBI Focused Fund secured an allocation worth Rs 315 crore, followed by BNP Paribas Financial Markets - ODI, which received shares valued at Rs 303.25 crore. Domestic mutual funds were allotted 2.489 crore shares worth Rs 2,784.96 crore, which is 34.34% of the anchor book. Several major international investment firms also participated in the anchor book. These included BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, Schroders, JPMorgan Asset Management, Franklin Templeton and Janus Henderson.

---

items.title: Jio Platforms IPO: QIB portion fully subscribed at nearly 2x
items.author: Paras Bisht
items.text:
Jio IPO subscription begins on October 21.

The Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) portion of the Jio Platforms Ltd’s IPO got fully subscribed at 1.95 times, according to the data available on NSE platform.

The Non Institutional Investors (NII) portion got booked 11 percent, while the retail portion saw a total demand of 8 percent.

Overall, the issue was subscribed by 56 percent, so far.

...

On October 19, Jio Platforms raised Rs 8,109.84 crore from 212 anchor investors, including BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity Investments, T. Rowe Price, Schroders, JPMorgan Asset Management, Franklin Templeton, Invesco, and Prudential. Anchor investors' demand for Jio Platforms’ IPO reached nearly Rs 2.5 lakh crore, making it the first Indian IPO to attract bids of this size.

...

8 ... Jio Platforms IPO details: The much-awaited IPO comprises a fresh issue of 27 crore equity shares, representing 2.9 percent of the company's post-issue equity capital. The issue includes a reservation of shares worth Rs 500 crore for Jio Platforms employees and Rs 2,500 crore worth of shares for eligible shareholders of its parent, Reliance Industries
